facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s presented with a slowly growing tumor on the scalp
otherwise healthy with no significant medical history
8-mm red, firm, mobile nodule on the left temporal scalp
irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels and absence of septa
Dermoscopic findings of scalp nodule
8-mm red nodule showing irregular red lacunae without septa and irregular linear vessels
Well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor extending to the superficial subcutaneous tissue
composed of ectatic thin-walled vessels with multiple intravascular branching papillary structures
Structures covered by swollen endothelial cells with numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules
Periodic acid−Schiff (PAS) staining showed positive hyaline globules in the cytoplasm of endothelial cells
Tumor vessels were positive for CD-31, negative for D2-40 (podoplanin) and HHV-8
α-smooth muscle actin highlighted the pericytes in the papillae

concepts.why: The patient's dermoscopic findings and histopathological results, including the presence of ectatic thin-walled vessels, intravascular branching papillary structures, and swollen endothelial cells with hyaline globules, are consistent with PILA.
The patient's clinical presentation, including a slowly growing tumor on the scalp with irregular red lacunae and absence of septa, is consistent with Hobnail Hemangioma.
The patient's presentation of a red, firm, mobile nodule on the scalp with dermoscopic findings of irregular red lacunae and irregular vessels is consistent with a vascular tumor.
The patient's clinical presentation, including a slowly growing tumor on the scalp with dermoscopic findings of irregular red lacunae and absence of septa, is consistent with a dermal vascular tumor.
